parsed.draft_response:
Hi there — thanks for flagging this. I’m sorry about the duplicate annual renewal charges.

We’ll need a quick bit more info to make sure we reverse the correct payment and confirm which invoice should stay in your accounting records:
1) The account identifier on the billing profile (your billing email / tenant ID)
2) For INV-9031 and INV-9032: the charged amounts and currency
3) The last 4 digits of the card (or payment method identifier) and/or the transaction IDs for each charge
4) Whether either invoice has already been refunded/adjusted (if you see a status in your billing portal)

Once we have that, our billing team will review the two charges and take the appropriate action to reverse the duplicate, then confirm which invoice (INV-9031 or INV-9032) should remain.

Please reply with the details above, and we’ll prioritize this as a high-urgency billing case.
promised_actions: Review the duplicate charges for the annual renewal
Reverse the duplicate charge once the correct payment is identified
Confirm whether INV-9031 or INV-9032 should remain in your accounting after review
safety_notes: Do not promise a refund without verifying which invoice is duplicate.
Avoid stating root cause; only say billing team will review.
Request minimal necessary identifiers to locate and distinguish the two transactions.

parsed.customer_impact: Customer was charged twice for an annual plan renewal and needs one charge reversed and the correct invoice identified for accounting.
grounded_facts: Customer reports their card was charged twice for the annual plan renewal on May 1.
Two invoice numbers are provided: INV-9031 and INV-9032.
Customer requests reversing one of the charges.
Customer requests confirmation of which invoice should remain in their accounting system.
missing_information: Card last 4 digits, payment method identifier, or transaction IDs for each of the two charges.
Amounts and currency of INV-9031 vs INV-9032.
Whether the charges have been captured/settled or are pending/refunded already.
Customer account identifier (email/tenant ID) and the subscription/plan name tied to the renewal.
Expected renewal date/amount per the billing system (to compare against the two invoices).
Any prior correspondence or billing reference number for this incident.
risk_signals: Billing/financial impact due to duplicate charges.
Ambiguity about which invoice is correct (INV-9031 vs INV-9032) could lead to incorrect accounting or missed refunds.
High urgency indicated by the customer’s request to reverse charges.
